title: Pace iteration is not single-knob: breach-semantics constants must be hand-scaled in lockstep across two files, but PR body invites one-line knob edits
evidence: _pr_body_pace.md:38: "one-line knob (150/180/240)." | data/packet_types.json:10: "latency_tol_ms": 2000, | data/packet_types.json:26: "latency_tol_ms": 1200, | data/balance.json:39: "exit_margin_ms": 160, | data/balance.json:2 (comment): "the 3.4 SLA tolerances + the E30 exit margin in packet_types.json/health scale with it to preserve semantics"
detail: Spec rule 1: 'single pace-scale knob ... we will iterate on the knobs'. A fun-test bump of packet_bandwidth alone (exactly what the PR body invites) stretches transits while the wall-time tolerances stay fixed, silently shifting breach semantics — the gameplay change the tuning forbids.
recommended_fix: Derive latency_tol_ms/exit_margin_ms from packet_bandwidth at load (or a shared pace-scale field), or amend the PR body/knob comments to state the 4-edit lockstep requirement for every pace iteration.

title: New fail-fast validation for terminal_spawn_interval_ticks/terminal_min_sep_tiles has zero negative tests; raised radius floor (4) also unpinned
detail: Project convention: 'Pin every design invariant as a regression test at the lowest layer'. Every other balance rule has fail-fast rows; the two new required-key branches and the raised floor (radius=4 now rejected, previously valid) are unpinned — a future regression passes silently.
recommended_fix: Add catalog_test fail-fast rows: each terminal knob missing, zero, negative, non-integer; and 'radius at new floor' (radius_tiles=4) pinning the terminal_min_sep_tiles=4 boundary.

title: sla_test breach/exit comments contradict the pinned assertions (1750 ms / 35 ticks / 8th-delivery window math vs pinned 1300 ms / tick 27 / 185)
detail: Stale draft comments: streaming long-path latency is 1300 ms (26 ticks) per the pins, not 1750/35; exit fires at the 2nd short delivery via cumulative average, not the 8th via window average. Misleads maintainers on both transit math and exit model.
recommended_fix: Rewrite the phase-1/phase-2 comments to match the pinned model: 26 ticks/1300 ms transit, cumulative-average exit at the 2nd short delivery (1150 ≤ 1200).

title: crisis_test re-stage prologues say '1/tick' seeds but the loops seed 0.5/tick with the opposite inline rationale
detail: Both re-staged crisis tests (resolve_and_retrigger, cooldown_gates_retrigger) carry prologue comments describing an abandoned 1/tick staging that contradicts the shipped 0.5/tick rate-ladder construction and its own inline rationale.
recommended_fix: Update both prologues to '0.5/tick (every 2nd tick) deterministic seeds' matching the loops.

title: Unused 'import "core:fmt"' added to warnings_test.odin — dead debug leftover in the diff
evidence: core/warnings_test.odin:23: "import \"core:fmt\"" — grep 'fmt' core/warnings_test.odin returns exactly one match (the import line itself); no 'fmt.' usage exists anywhere in the file (odin test core passes, so it is dead, not used).
detail: The diff adds an import with zero usages — a leftover from a debug session (likely a removed fmt.println). Unexplained dead code in the shipped change; -vet hygiene would flag it.
